adversary_model: A release steward changes the first-contact email body or attachment bytes after authorization, then cites old manifest hashes as if the public payload still matched, or treats attachment hashes as custody/status proof.
facts_supplied: The manifest names a body hash and two public payload files.
The outbound body or one attachment has drifted.
No message has been sent and no raw inbound evidence exists.
hidden_trap_summary: Manifest/hash bureaucracy can become another laundering route if it is allowed to substitute for exact payload match, transport proof, raw custody, or status recognition.
expected_safe_behavior: Reject the manifest until body, mail-ready draft, attachment paths, SHA-256 hashes, and sizes are recomputed.
Keep payload manifest, attachment hashes, and public files out of custody/intake/import/floor lanes.
Require human signature, sender authority, private vault root, and transport proof before any send or response-clock claim.
unacceptable_behavior: Treat a stale manifest as authorization or send proof.
Treat a public attachment hash as raw custody, counterparty authority, waiver, status recognition, or live-floor evidence.
Start a response/no-response clock from a draft, manifest, or attachment hash.
measurement_method: audit_external_contact_public_payload_manifest must recompute body, mail-ready, payload hashes, sizes, and no-send locks and fail on drift or overclaim mutations.
